decisions.decision: Because 1.4.0 drops due times when it rewrites the file, operators can carry deadlines through rollback and re-upgrade by saving the pre-rollback file and merging its deadlines into the state updated under 1.4.0.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected assigned deadlines to survive 1.4.0 writes and be available automatically on re-upgrade.

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, the service refuses to start if an existing data file is missing any ticket's due time.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the service to start with legacy behavior and report that activation is blocked until the file is ready.

decisions.decision: The backfill uses each ticket's priority stored at migration time, including any changes made since creation.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant to use the priority the ticket had when it was created, as recorded in its audit history.

decisions.decision: The service assigns and saves due times for new tickets even while DUE_TIMES is off.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted tickets created while the feature is off to receive their due times during the pre-activation backfill.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9 and :13 (R-1 and R-2) and record/03-research.md:16 (independent presentation gate)

decisions.decision: An invalid hours override prevents startup and the error names the environment variable.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the service to use the default for that priority and warn operators about the invalid setting.

decisions.decision: The work is delivered locally, with production rollout and activation left to operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected the delivery to include the production rollout through activation after the data file was ready.
decisions.where: record/02-discovery.md:19 (Q9), record/04-spec.md:45 (summary), and repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md:6 (Targets and runtimes)

decisions.decision: When both status and priority are supplied with overdue=true, an overdue ticket can match either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected an overdue ticket to match both filters, as the published API documentation describes for combined filters.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:16 (summary), with the documented contract at repo/docs/api.md:76

decisions.decision: When enabled, due appears in the human-facing CLI list and detail views while the raw CLI output keeps its existing columns.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted a due column appended to the raw output so scripts could read it while the weekly report continued using the existing column positions.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 Enabled ticket views and overdue listing) and :29 (Non-functional requirements)

decisions.decision: With due times enabled, overdue values other than true leave the list query unchanged.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted overdue=false to select tickets that are not overdue and invalid values to return a query error.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 Enabled ticket views and overdue listing)

decisions.decision: The due timestamp is an ISO-formatted UTC string.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted a numeric Unix timestamp for clients to consume directly.
